John F. Kennedy was the first Roman Catholic ever elected president of the United States [d8][d9][d3]. He narrowly defeated Republican Vice President Richard M. Nixon in the 1960 presidential election, becoming both the first Catholic and the youngest person ever elected to the office [d8]. Kennedy had faced significant anti-Catholic prejudice during his campaign, as only one Catholic (Al Smith) had previously been nominated by a major party, and Smith lost in 1928 [d1][d6]. Kennedy remained the only Catholic president until Joe Biden was sworn in on January 20, 2021 [d2].
